session2_findings.host: Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL (4 vCPU), onnxruntime 1.31 (and 1.18.0 where noted); measured, not projected

1_runtime_blocker_fixed.finding: Session-1 INT8 encoder and INT8 VITS use ConvInteger with int8 weights; onnxruntime 1.18.0-1.22.0 (the APK ships 1.18.0) raise NOT_IMPLEMENTED at load, i.e. STT and TTS would have failed on the phone.
1_runtime_blocker_fixed.fix: encoder re-quantized MatMul-only (convs fp32); VITS shipped fp16-stored/fp32-computed; every graph gated by speech_lab/check_ort_compat.py under onnxruntime==1.18.0 (see ort_runtime_compat)

2_tts_int8_vs_fp16_storage.decision: ship vaani_tts_vits.fp16.onnx (3.2x faster than INT8, loads on ORT 1.18)

3_tied_embedding_logits_fusion.finding: community INT8 decoders compute logits as MatMul(h, DequantizeLinear(Transpose(W_q))) and ORT never constant-folds DequantizeLinear: every step de-quantised the 51865x384 table (16.7 of 28.7 ms/step)
3_tied_embedding_logits_fusion.fix: prepare_models.fuse_tied_logits_int8 -> com.microsoft.DynamicQuantizeMatMul on one shared transposed table

4_kv_cache_exactness.int8_decoders: 2/12 identical: dynamic per-tensor activation scales differ between a full-prefix pass and a 1-token pass (inherent to dynamic quantization, not a cache bug)

5_stt_precision_study_cer_forced_languag.decision: ship INT8 enc+dec for latency; fp16-stored encoder (16.5 MB) is the first knob for Hinglish accuracy

suppress_latin_tokens_in_hi_mode.note: Whisper-tiny degenerates into CJK fragments / digit loops

session2_findings.8_gemini_model_retirement: gemini-2.5-flash -> HTTP 404 'no longer available to new users'; app uses gemini-3.5-flash-lite (thinkingLevel=minimal) with automatic 404/429/503 fallback

1_llm_failover_cascade.failover_triggers: any HTTP error, network error, no first token within 4000 ms, or an empty reply - only before the first token (a started reply is never restarted on another model); a network error skips that provider's remaining rungs for the turn

cooldowns_ms.429: Retry-After header (Groq) or RetryInfo.retryDelay (Gemini), else 60000; capped at 1800000

free_tier_limits_observed.groq_each_model: 1000 requests/day, 8000 tokens/min (x-ratelimit-limit-* headers); one turn ~1000 tokens
free_tier_limits_observed.gemini-3.5-flash: 20 requests/day: HTTP 429 quotaId GenerateRequestsPerDayPerProjectPerModel-FreeTier (metric reported for gemini-3.6-flash), retryDelay 41108 s at 12:33 UTC -> resets ~07:00 UTC

1_llm_failover_cascade.session2_429_diagnosis: the Session-2 gemini-3.5-flash 429s were this DAILY cap (20/day), not a per-minute window
1_llm_failover_cascade.unit_tests: LlmStreamingClientTest: 17 MockWebServer tests (cross-provider failover, every pre-token HTTP code, first-token timeout, empty reply, cool-down skip + reset, keyless rungs, mid-stream error not retried)

2_encoder_precision_paired_ab.method: paired: 12 utterances x 6 seeded VITS samples (seed 1234); every encoder transcribes the identical audio/mel; same INT8 decoders + KV cache; paired deltas = mean(other - base) with 95% bootstrap CI over utterance-samples; encoder_ms on this host with onnxruntime 1.31.0
2_encoder_precision_paired_ab.finding: fp16-stored and fp32 encoders decode token-identically to each other; vs INT8 the Hinglish CER change is -0.0135 with a 95% CI spanning zero (13 better / 18 worse pairs). The INT8 encoder's quantisation is NOT what limits Hinglish accuracy.
2_encoder_precision_paired_ab.decision: keep vaani_stt_encoder.int8.onnx (11.7 MB, fastest). No encoder meets 120 ms on this 2-core host; Whisper always encodes a 30 s window.

3_decode_language_token.script: speech_lab/decode_language_ab.py (seed 1234, 6 Hinglish corpus utterances x 6 samples)
3_decode_language_token.decision: keep <|hi|>: <|en|> translates/hallucinates Hinglish audio even more

4_hinglish_post_corrector.what: HinglishCodec.normalizeSttTranscript/displayTranscript: phonetic lexicon (curated variants + Hinglish phonetic key, unique matches only, never rewrites real English/CMU words), DP compound splitter (2-3 known words), context rules (kaal->kal by a time word; sate/seat/sat->set by alarm/reminder or karna; number word before baje -> digits; 'baje kal alarm' -> 'baje ka alarm'), split-word merges, domain spellings

closed_loop_effect.what: paired raw -> display CER on the same transcripts (auto language, Latin-script raw output only, so both sides are scored against the same Roman reference)

4_hinglish_post_corrector.unit_tests: HinglishCodecTest: 10 post-corrector tests incl. clean EN/Hinglish left untouched and a <500 us/transcript timing test
4_hinglish_post_corrector.limitation: most remaining Hinglish error is Whisper-tiny translating or hallucinating (e.g. 'Today's schedule is our next meeting.'), which no lexicon can repair; the corrector deliberately leaves English sentences alone

5_release_build.r8: isMinifyEnabled + isShrinkResources; keeps: in.iisc.vaani.dsp.** (JNI), ai.onnxruntime.**, @Keep, in.iisc.vaani.llm.**, config data classes
5_release_build.signing: local PKCS12 keystore outside the repo (/tmp/vaani_release.jks), credentials only in git-ignored local.properties; falls back to the debug key when absent
5_release_build.side_by_side: debug installs as in.iisc.vaani.debug ('VaaniEdge (debug)'), release as in.iisc.vaani

6_heldout_lid.errors: H6-en 'Wake me up at 6:30 AM tomorrow.' -> hi in 5/6 samples (p_hi 0.77-0.98); H7-en -> hi in 1/6
6_heldout_lid.mitigation: manual language override (Auto / English / Hinglish chip); the post-corrector leaves English text unchanged even under a hi label

session3_findings.7_lab_bridge_bug_found_and_fixed: SttDisplayExportTest initially ran without the CMU lexicon (the app always installs it), so the fuzzy phonetic key rewrote English 'say' -> 'se'; fixed by installing the lexicon in the bridge and by making the codec skip all fuzzy matching when no English lexicon is present (unit test added); display CER re-scored with verify_closed_loop.py --rescore-display
session3_findings.host_note: latency figures from the Session-3 closed-loop run were taken while a remote-desktop session shared the 4 vCPUs; models/runtime/session options are unchanged since Session 2, so compare latency across sessions with care (the encoder A/B ran back-to-back under equal conditions)
